title: Account types, interest and charges
blurb: Savings or current? Zero-balance? Fixed or recurring deposit? Learn what each one does, with the numbers.
t1.title: Savings or current?
t1.hook: Ravi saves pocket money. His uncle runs a kirana shop and banks the shop takings. They need different kinds of account.
t1.define: A **savings account** is for personal money you keep and add to. It pays interest. A **current account** is for a business with many payments each day.
t1.analogy: A savings account is like your own cupboard at home. A current account is like the shop counter, always busy with money moving in and out.
q1.prompt: Ravi's uncle takes many payments in and out of his shop each day. Which account type is made for that?
q1.hint: Which one is for a business?
q1.explain: A current account is built for the many daily payments of a business.
q2.prompt: Which account usually pays interest to a student who is just saving?
q2.hint: Think about who the account is for.
q2.explain: A savings account is meant for saving and normally pays interest.
t2.title: Interest on savings
t2.define: The bank adds interest to a savings account. A higher balance earns more interest at the same rate.
t2.formula: Interest = balance × rate × years. A rate of 3% a year is 0.03 in the formula.
t2.steps.1: Meena keeps {exBal} in a savings account.
t2.steps.2: The rate is {rate} a year, for {years1} year.
q3.prompt: Ravi keeps {qBal} for {years1} year at {rate} a year. How much interest does he earn? Type a number in rupees.
q4.prompt: Asha doubles her balance and keeps the same rate and time. What happens to her interest?
q4.hint: Look at the formula: balance is one of the numbers multiplied.
q4.explain: Interest grows with the balance, so doubling the balance doubles the interest.
t3.title: Minimum balance and charges
t3.define: Some accounts ask you to keep a **minimum balance**. If your balance falls below it, the bank may charge you.
t3.mistake: Many people think the minimum balance is a fee they pay. It is not. It is money that stays yours. Only the charge for going below it is a cost.
t3.steps.1: The account asks for a minimum balance of {minBal}.
t3.steps.2: Ravi's balance falls to {raviBal}, which is below the minimum.
t3.steps.3: The bank charges {chargeEach} each month he stays below.
q5.prompt: The minimum is {minBal}. Ravi has {raviBal}. How much is he short? Type a number in rupees.
q5.hint: Take his balance away from the minimum.
q6.hint: Does the money leave your account?
q6.explain: It is an amount you keep in the account. You pay a charge only if you fall below it.
q6.opt.a: An amount to keep in the account to avoid a charge
q6.fb.b: The minimum balance is your own money, kept in the account. It is not a fee. Only the charge for dipping below it is.
q7.prompt: Ravi stays below the minimum for {chargeMonths} months at {chargeEach} a month. What is the total charge? Type a number in rupees.
q7.hint: Multiply the charge by the months.
t4.title: Lab: balance, rate and the minimum
t4.explore: Open the lab. Change the balance and the rate. See the yearly interest, and whether you are above or below the minimum.
q8.prompt: In the lab, set the balance to {labBal} and the rate to {labRate}. What is the interest in a year? Type a number in rupees.
q8.hint: Read "Interest in a year" in the lab.
q9.prompt: In the lab, the last number is below zero. What does that tell you?
q9.hint: It compares your balance to the minimum.
q9.explain: A number below zero means the balance is under the minimum, so a charge may apply.
q9.opt.a: The balance is below the minimum
t5.title: Zero-balance, fixed and recurring deposits
t5.define: A **zero-balance account** asks for no minimum. A **fixed deposit** locks one lump sum for a set time at a set rate. A **recurring deposit** takes the same amount every month.
t5.tradeoff: The fixed rate is certain, but your money is locked. Taking it out early usually costs you part of the interest.
q10.prompt: Meena puts {fdAmt} in a fixed deposit at {fdRate} for {years1} year. How much interest does she earn? Type a number in rupees.
q10.hint: Use the interest formula: amount times rate times years.
q11.prompt: Asha pays {rdMonthly} into a recurring deposit for {rdMonths} months. How much does she pay in all? Type a number in rupees.
q11.hint: Multiply the monthly amount by the months.
q12.prompt: Ravi locks money in a fixed deposit for a year. What is true?
q12.explain: The money is locked until the end of the term. Early withdrawal usually costs part of the interest.
q12.opt.a: The money is locked for the term
q12.opt.b: He can always withdraw it free any day
q12.fb.b: A fixed deposit is not like a savings account. Taking money out early usually costs you interest.
q12.opt.d: It needs no money to start
glossary.bank_savings_account.def: An account for personal money that pays interest.
glossary.bank_current_account.def: A business account made for many payments each day.
glossary.bank_min_balance.def: The amount you must keep in an account to avoid a charge.
glossary.bank_fixed_deposit.def: A lump sum locked for a set time at a set rate.
glossary.bank_recurring_deposit.def: A fixed amount saved every month for a set time.
glossary.bank_zero_balance.def: An account that needs no minimum balance.
